subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` adopt a permanent 1 MiB public input limit, or should the implementation bound memory without rejecting previously accepted large regular files?
rationale: The proposed limit is a new user-visible failure mode rather than a mechanically implied safety fix, and current PR evidence does not establish a prior published limit or an owner-approved compatibility policy.

options.title: Preserve compatibility with bounded reading
options.body: Implement streaming or another bounded-memory approach that continues to accept existing regular body files, then add regression coverage and real CLI proof.

options.title: Adopt and document the 1 MiB contract
options.body: Approve the fixed limit explicitly, document its user-facing implications and upgrade behavior, and retain the rejection tests and real CLI proof.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Close or defer this PR if neither a compatible implementation nor an approved permanent limit is currently desired.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility with bounded reading
recommendation.body: Implement streaming or another bounded-memory approach that continues to accept existing regular body files, then add regression coverage and real CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The review timeline specifically routes the unresolved memory-wiki contract question to this participant, though source-history confirmation was unavailable.
